questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was crucial that the exchange destination was different from what I am used to in Denmark - when it comes to for instance religion, culture, language, landscape, architecture etc. I wanted to be taken out of my comfort zone and explore new things that could feed my curiosity. Moreover i chose the destination because of my academic interest in urban sociology, and Istanbul is such an interesting city in the eyes of an urban sociologist.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was actually a bit difficult. It was hard to get in touch with the Istanbul Bilgi Office.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were assisted online (1 online class), and then I got a local buddy from the same department as mine, so if I were unsure about something/ needed to use a local phone number or just couldn't find my way around I could reach out to my buddy. Additionally they had an Erasmus Office at Santral Campus where they were helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I am not aware of anyone who stayed at the campus housing. Some people lived there for the first month, but since it's not in the most interesting part of the city, everyone that I know of moved to beyoglu

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I found a place in Cihangir on Airbnb (fair price) and had the best experience. I choose to do it this way since I wanted to stay with some local people. I can definitely recommend this area. 
Important: when choosing where to stay you should check out the modes of transportaion for the campus and count on it taken a little longer than Google Maps states.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The system is very logical. The exchange students were (by default, I hope) given access to the system later than the ordinary students, so when I finally got access all of my planned courses were already full and closed for registration, but I ended up with some good alternative courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You are given the contact information for a teacher in your department, whom you can contact. Moreover you have your buddy, who is more han familiar with the system

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not succesfull at all. They were all closed for registration or had requirements that I was not aware of.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the time of registration, so you can access the system as the exact time the registration starts. If your classes are "closed for registration" don't hesitate writing an email to the professor and ask for special permission - this helped me get in to several classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was a BA student at Copenhagen at the time of exchange and at Bilgi University I took classes on nearly all levels (first year, second year, third year and master).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Smaller classes, less of an like "lecture" vibe. I had to pretty involved in all of the sociology classes, but since it was so interesting it was not a problem, and the environment between professors and students were very relaxed so it seemed natural to contribute, ask questions etc.
Most of my exams were 2-hour hand written exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Change in Contemporary Turkish Society
Social Inequality
Art, ecology and society
Basics of sociology
Psychology of learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend taking classes with Firat Genc (Social inequality & Change n Contemporary Turkish society). He is such an inspiring urban sociologist and a very good and passionate teacher. If you can only chose one, you should take the class "change in contemporary turkish society".

questions.answer: So many different activities - ranging from ceramics to ultimate

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Not hosted by the university, but I would definietly recommend to travel around Turkey whenever possible. It is such a diverse and beautiful country.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Istanbul has an amazing food scene - take adavntage of the cheap prices and try some of the top restaurants (Neolokal, Aheste, Mikla etc.). Take a one-day-trip to the Princess Islands. Walk around the neighborhoods of Kadikoy and along the waterfront there is a cool park - great for relaxing. Istanbul is full of different neighborhoods, which is represents something totally different. Take one neighborhood at a time and see how the life changes, how all women wears scarfs one place (e.g. Fatih) and none another place (e.g. Moda), how you can drink alcohol at every corner in Cihangir or Moda, when you are not allowed to serve in Balat etc. Take the ferries as much as possible - especially during the golden hour. You can also take the ferry (2 hour) on a weekend trip to Bursa for hiking and seeing an old and beautiful city center. 

Moreover it is easy to travel around turkey by bus. I went to Sinop - Ankara - Cappadocia - Pamukkale - Kusadasi - Ephesus - Izmir - Ayvalik, and I can recommend all of these places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I need to be extremely observant of how others were behaving, talking, dressing, but it was not uncomfortable

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: live with them!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: gender stereotypes and the political vulnerability

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: religion, food and everything else

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I think that I have expressed many of the things in the above listed sections - but you shpuld really look forward to seeing the city - it's just breathtaking.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of right now

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Traveling around Turkey, living with a local Turkish guy and a Syrian refugee and just walking around the beautiful city each day.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
